title: Understanding Zero-One Loss
text: The zero-one loss function is used to measure the accuracy of predictions. It assigns a loss of $$1$$ for each incorrect prediction and $$0$$ for each correct prediction.

title: Calculate Predicted Labels
text: Given the predicted probabilities $$(0.1$$, $$0.6$$, $$0.9)$$ and the threshold $$T=0.5$$, determine the predicted labels (0 or 1) for each instance.

title: Determine Predicted Labels
text: For each predicted probability, compare it to the threshold $$T=0.5$$. If the probability is greater than T, the predicted label is 1; otherwise, it is $$0$$.

title: Compare True and Predicted Labels
text: Now that you have the predicted labels, compare them with the true labels (0,0,1) to determine if each prediction is correct or incorrect.

title: Calculate Zero-One Loss
text: For each instance, check if the true label matches the predicted label. If they do not match, assign a loss of $$1$$. Sum the losses to get the total zero-one loss.
